source_text:
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, ποιήσωμεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ καλέσαντος ἡμᾶς, ἵνα ζήσωμεν, καὶ διώξωμεν μᾶλλον τὴν ἀρετήν, τὴν δὲ κακίαν καταλείψωμεν ὡς προοδοιπόρον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, καὶ φύγωμεν τὴν ἀσέβειαν, μὴ ἡμᾶς καταλάβῃ κακά.
ἐὰν γὰρ σπουδάσωμεν ἀγαθοποιεῖν, διώξεται ἡμᾶς εἰρήνη.
διὰ ταύτην γὰρ τὴν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἄνθρωπον, οἵτινες παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους, προῃρημένοι μᾶλλον τὴν ἐνθάδε ἀπόλαυσιν ἡ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπαγγελίαν.
ἀγνοοῦσιν γὰρ ἡλίκην ἔχει βάσανον ἡ ἐνθάδε ἀπόλαυσις, καὶ οἵαν τρυφὴν ἔχει ἡ μέλλουσα ἐπαγγελία.
καὶ εἰ μὲν αὐτοὶ μόνοι ταῦτα ἔπρασσον, ἀνεκτὸν ἦν: νῦν δὲ ἐπιμένουσιν κακοδιδασκαλοῦντες τὰς ἀναιτίους ψυχάς, οὐκ εἰδότες, ὅτι δισσὴν ἕξουσιν τὴν κρίσιν, αὐτοί τε καὶ οἱ ἀκούοντες αὐτῶν.
thought_title: Pursue virtue, flee evil, and shun false teachers
orientation: The preacher is exhorting the congregation to do God's will and warns against those who prefer present pleasure to the coming promise.
pass_a_gloss: So then, my brothers, let us do the will of the Father who called us, so that we may live, and let us pursue rather virtue, and let us abandon evil as [the] forerunner of our sins, and let us flee impiety, lest evils overtake us. For if we are eager to do good, peace will pursue us. For because of this reason it is not possible to find a human being, who pass along human fears, having chosen rather the here pleasure than the coming promise. For they do not know how great torment the here pleasure has, and what kind of delight the coming promise has. And if they alone were doing these things, it would be bearable; but now they persist in teaching badly the innocent souls, not knowing that they will have double judgment, both they themselves and those who hear them.

choices.why: The image is of evil walking ahead and leading the way into sin; 'forerunner' preserves the path metaphor.
The adverb ἐνθάδε contrasts with the coming promise; 'here' keeps the spatial contrast sharp.
The verb suggests spreading or transmitting fears from one person to another; 'pass along' captures the contagious sense.
The adjective δισσήν means twofold; 'double judgment' is the plain rendering.
The imperfect with the conditional particle marks an unreal condition; 'would be bearable' preserves the counterfactual force.

pass_b_english: So then, my brothers, let us do the will of the Father who called us, so that we may live. Let us pursue virtue instead, and abandon evil as the forerunner of our sins. Let us flee from ungodliness, so that no evil overtakes us.
For if we are eager to do good, peace will pursue us.
For this reason no one can be found who is free from human fears, since they have chosen the pleasure here rather than the coming promise.
They do not know how much torment the pleasure here holds, and what delight the coming promise holds.

If they alone were doing these things, it would be bearable. But now they persist in leading blameless souls astray by their teaching, not knowing that they will have a twofold judgment, both themselves and those who listen to them.

problems.why: Word order is awkward; 'teaching badly' is too weak for κακοδιδασκαλοῦντες ('maligning' or 'leading astray by teaching'); ἀναιτίους means 'blameless' or 'innocent' but the syntax is broken
problems.fix: persist in leading astray by teaching the blameless souls

problems.why: 'instead' adds contrast not in source; μᾶλλον means 'rather' or 'more', not 'instead'

problems.quote: no one can be found who passes along human fears
problems.source_quote: οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἄνθρωπον, οἵτινες παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους
problems.why: παράγουσι means 'lead astray' or 'mislead', not 'pass along'; φόβους here means 'terrors' or 'dread things' that mislead, not 'fears' transmitted
problems.fix: no one can be found who leads astray with human terrors

problems.why: δισσὴν means 'twofold' or 'double' in the sense of 'for two parties', but 'double judgment' could mean two judgments; 'twofold judgment' or 'judgment on two counts' is clearer

edits.old: Let us pursue virtue instead, and abandon evil as the forerunner of our sins.
edits.new: Let us rather pursue virtue, and abandon evil as the forerunner of our sins.

edits.new: This is the reason no one can be found who leads astray with human terrors: they have chosen the pleasure here rather than the coming promise.

edits.old: But now they persist in teaching badly the innocent souls, not knowing that they will have double judgment—both themselves and those who listen to them.
edits.new: But now they persist in leading astray by teaching the blameless souls, not knowing that they will have twofold judgment—both themselves and those who listen to them.

fixed: The 'double judgment' problem is fixed by changing to 'twofold judgment' in the same edit as the 'teaching badly' fix.

problems.why: παράγουσι means 'produce/introduce' fears, not 'lead astray'; sense is people who incite human fears (to deter believers)
problems.fix: no one can be found who incites human terrors

problems.quote: no one can be found who incites human terrors
problems.source_quote: οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἄνθρωπον, οἵτινες παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους
problems.why: παράγουσι means 'lead astray/away', not 'incite'; φόβους here means 'fears/anxieties', not 'terrors'. Sense is 'lead into human fears/anxieties'.
problems.fix: no one can be found who leads others into human anxieties
problems.ruling: παράγουσι means 'lead/bring'; 'incite' misleads. φόβους = 'fears', not 'terrors'. Combined error changes meaning.

problems.fix: Standardize to one form throughout, or note that all forms address the same congregation.

problems.why: 'Human fears' does not fit the context about people choosing pleasure over promise; the Greek likely means 'human opinions' or 'human anxieties.'

fixed: The 'brothers' note is a style observation, not a mistranslation; the English uses 'brothers' consistently and the source uses ἀδελφοί μου, so no edit is needed.

The Greek παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους means 'they pass along human fears' or 'they lead others into human fears/anxieties'; the English 'when they bring in human fears' misstates the source, so I changed it to 'no one can be found who leads others into human anxieties' to match the Greek more closely while keeping the sentence natural.

problems.quote: no one can be found who leads others into human anxieties
problems.why: The sentence does not make sense as English; 'no one can be found who leads' is garbled.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'those who lead others into worldly anxieties cannot be found [doing good].'

edits.new: This is the reason no one can be found who leads others into human anxieties, having chosen the pleasure here rather than the coming promise.

fixed: The source reads: διὰ ταύτην γὰρ τὴν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἄνθρωπον, οἵτινες παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους, προῃρημένοι μᾶλλον τὴν ἐνθάδε ἀπόλαυσιν ἡ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπαγγελίαν. The English 'no one can be found who leads others into human anxieties' is a faithful rendering of οὐκ ἔστιν εὑρεῖν ἄνθρωπον, οἵτινες παράγουσι φόβους ἀνθρωπίνους. The reported problem is a style objection, not a mistranslation. I made the smallest change to improve flow by converting the colon clause into a participial phrase, matching the source's προῃρημένοι.

problems.quote: This is the reason no one can be found who prefers the pleasure here to the coming promise and yet leads others into human fears.
problems.why: The sentence is syntactically broken; the logical connection between preferring pleasure and leading into fears is unclear.

edits.old: This is the reason no one can be found who prefers the pleasure here to the coming promise and yet leads others into human fears.

fixed: The English sentence was syntactically broken and misstated the source's causal structure. The source says: 'For because of this reason it is not possible to find a human being, who pass along human fears, having chosen rather the here pleasure than the coming promise.' The participle 'having chosen' (προῃρημένοι) modifies the people who pass along human fears, not a separate clause. The fix restores the participial structure and the correct contrast between 'the pleasure here' and 'the coming promise.'

polish.changed: Clarified the final sentence by making the subject of the teaching explicit and smoothing the word order, so the twofold judgment reads naturally and the contrast between the present pleasure and the coming promise is easier to follow aloud.

Clarified the garbled sentence about human fears by reordering it so the preference for present pleasure is clearly the cause of leading others astray, and made the contrast between present pleasure and the coming promise flow naturally.
